title: Memory and Age
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.answer: C — Experience-based strategies can make older people more efficient.
questions.answerKey: C — Experience-based strategies can make older people more efficient.
questions.prompt: What does the typists’ experiment show?
questions.translation: 打字員實驗顯示了甚麼？

blocks.text: “At the Georgia Institute of Technology, psychologist Timothy Salthouse, Ph.D., compared a group of very fast and accurate typists of college age with another group in their 60s.”
在 Georgia Institute of Technology，心理學家 Timothy Salthouse 比較了一組年輕、打字很快且準確的大學生打字員，以及另一組六十多歲的打字員。
“The neural networks involved in typing appear to have been reshaped to compensate for losses in motor skills or other age changes.”
參與打字的 neural networks 似乎已被重新塑造，用來補償 motor skills 或其他年齡變化造成的損失。
只看首尾句，Paragraph C 的功能已很清楚：它用 typists experiment 比較年輕人和老年人的表現，並指出老年人可能透過補償方式維持效率。題目直接問 typists’ experiment show，因此Paragraph C 是目標段落。
掃描時最有用的是 “typists” 和 “in their 60s”。這兩個詞能迅速帶到 Paragraph C。真正決定答案的是 “strategies” 和 “efficient”。

“The older typists, it turned out, achieved their speed with cunning little strategies that made them far more efficient than their younger counterparts: They made fewer finger movements, saving a fraction of a second here and there. They also read ahead in the text.”
結果發現，年長打字員靠一些巧妙的小策略達到速度，這些策略令他們比年輕對手更有效率：他們手指動作較少，這裡那裡各省下一點時間。他們也會預先閱讀後面的文字。
這句的主語是 “The older typists”。核心動詞是 “achieved their speed”，方法是 “with cunning little strategies”。結果是 “made them far more efficient”。後面兩個例子清楚說明策略內容：減少手指動作、預先閱讀文字。
選項 C 說 “Experience-based strategies can make older people more efficient.”這正好概括原文：年長打字員靠策略補償年齡相關損失。這些策略很可能來自長期打字經驗，所以 “experience-based” 合理。
選項排除A Older people’s reading ability is superior.原文只說 older typists “read ahead in the text”，即打字時預讀後文。這不等於整體 reading ability superior。選項把一個打字策略擴大成一般閱讀能力優勢。
B Age-related losses are irreversible. Paragraph C 的方向相反：原文說 neural networks reshaped to compensate，即有補償空間。它沒有說所有 age-related losses 都不可逆。
D Older people perform poorly in driving tests.原文完全沒有 driving tests。這是無關選項。

questions.answer: D — Boring and stimulating surroundings affect brain development.
questions.answerKey: D — Boring and stimulating surroundings affect brain development.
questions.prompt: Which statement about the rat experiment is correct?
questions.translation: 關於 rat experiment，哪一個說法正確？

blocks.text: “When a rat is kept in isolation without playmates or objects to interact with, the animal’s brain shrinks, but if we put that rat with 11 other rats in a large cage and give them an assortment of wheels, ladders, and other toys, we can show—after four days—significant differences in its brain,” says Diamond, professor of integrative biology.
Diamond 說，若一隻老鼠被單獨飼養，沒有玩伴，也沒有可互動的物件，牠的大腦會縮小；但若把牠和另外 11 隻老鼠放在大籠中，並給牠們各種 wheels、ladders 和其他 toys，四天後便可看到牠的大腦有顯著差異。最後一句：“Animals are just like we are. They need stimulation,” says Diamond.
Diamond 說，動物和我們一樣。牠們需要刺激。首尾句都圍繞 isolation、toys、stimulation、brain differences。這段就是 rat experiment 的目標段落。
“assortment of wheels, ladders, and other toys”
“boring surroundings” 在原文不一定逐字出現，但 isolation、沒有玩伴、沒有可互動物件，以及toys 要 varied，全部屬於單調或刺激不足的環境。

關鍵原文：“Proliferating dendrites first appear in the visual association areas. After a month in the enriched environment, the whole cerebral cortex has expanded, as has its blood supply. Even in the enriched environment, rats get bored unless the toys are varied.”
增生的 dendrites 先出現在 visual association areas。一個月後，在 enriched environment 中，整個 cerebral cortex 已擴大，血液供應也增加。即使在豐富環境中，若玩具沒有變化，老鼠也會感到厭倦。

選項 D 說 “Boring and stimulating surroundings affect brain development.”原文同時提供兩邊證據：isolation 令 brain shrinks；enriched environment 令 dendrites、cerebral cortex 和 blood supply 增加。最後 “rats get bored unless the toys are varied” 也支援 boring surroundings 會影響刺激程度。
選項排除A Different toys have different effects on rats.原文說 toys 要 varied，因為 rats get bored。它沒有比較 wheels、ladders、other toys 各自造成不同腦部效果。
B The rats’ brains increased in weight in both cages.原文沒有說 brain weight，也沒有說 both cages 都增加。isolated rat 的 brain shrinks。
C The isolated rats’ brains grew new connections.新 dendrites 出現在 enriched environment 的描述中，不在 isolated condition。

questions.answer: B — Their chess knowledge was better organised.
questions.answerKey: B — Their chess knowledge was better organised.
questions.prompt: What conclusion can be drawn from the study involving children who played chess?
questions.translation: 從 children who played chess 的研究可得出甚麼結論？

blocks.text: “‘You could say metamemory is a byproduct of going to school,’ says psychologist Robert Kail, Ph.D., of Purdue University, who studies children from birth to 20 years, the time of life when mental development is most rapid.”
Purdue University 的心理學家 Robert Kail 說，可以說 metamemory 是上學的副產品；他研究從出生到 20 歲的 children，這是 mental development 最快的人生階段。

“‘Because they’d played a lot of chess, their knowledge of chess was better organized than that of the adults, and their existing knowledge of chess served as a framework for new memory,’ explains Kail.”
Kail 解釋，因為他們下了很多棋，所以他們的 chess knowledge 比成年人組織得更好；他們已有的 chess knowledge 成為新記憶的框架。
首尾句顯示 Paragraph I 的功能：已有知識和教育經驗會影響記憶。題目問 children chess study的結論，最後一句直接提供答案。
“their knowledge of chess was better organized”
“child experts” 是最強定位詞，因為題目說 children who played chess。
關鍵原文：“But when asked to remember the patterns of chess pieces arranged on a board, the children won.”
但當他們被要求記住棋盤上棋子的排列模式時，孩子勝出。
“Because they’d played a lot of chess, their knowledge of chess was better organized than that of the adults, and their existing knowledge of chess served as a framework for new memory,”
因為他們下了很多棋，所以他們的 chess knowledge 比成年人組織得更好；他們已有的 chess knowledge 為新記憶提供框架。
題目問 “What conclusion can be drawn?” 正確答案必須解釋孩子為何在棋盤記憶上勝出。原文不是說孩子一般記憶更好，因為同段前面說 random series of numbers 測試中 adults outscored the children。孩子只在 chess patterns 中勝出，原因是已有 chess knowledge 更有組織。
選項排除A They beat the adults at chess.原文沒有說孩子和 adults 真正下棋比賽。測試內容是記住 chess pieces patterns。
C Their visual memory was better than the adults’.孩子勝出的是 chess-specific memory，不是 general visual memory。原文把原因放在 organized chess knowledge。
D They used a different part of the brain while playing chess.原文沒有提到 brain part，也沒有 brain imaging。

questions.answer: C — Vocabulary, as a form of crystallised intelligence, declines very little with age.
questions.answerKey: C — Vocabulary, as a form of crystallised intelligence, declines very little with age.
questions.prompt: Why does the author refer to vocabulary research at the end of the passage?
questions.translation: 作者為何在文章結尾提到 vocabulary research？

blocks.text: “Specialized knowledge is a mental resource that only improves with time.”
專門知識是一種只會隨時間改善的 mental resource。

“Retired professionals, especially teachers and journalists, consistently score higher on tests of vocabulary and general information than college students, who are supposed to be in their mental prime.”
退休專業人士，尤其教師和記者，在 vocabulary 和 general information tests 中，通常比被認為處於智力黃金期的大學生得分更高。
只看首尾句，Paragraph J 的結尾例子並非孤立資料。它用 vocabulary research 支持段落主旨： specialized knowledge / crystallized intelligence 可隨時間累積，年長者在某些知識型能力上仍然很強。
“Vocabulary is one such specialized form of accrued knowledge”
題目問 why，所以要看例子前的主題句。最重要的是 “Vocabulary is one such specialized form of accrued knowledge.”
“Crystallized intelligence about one’s occupation apparently does not decline at all until at least age 75, and if there is no disease or dementia, may remain even longer.”
一個人與職業相關的 crystallized intelligence 顯然至少到 75 歲前完全不會下降；如果沒有疾病或 dementia，可能保持更久。
“Vocabulary is one such specialized form of accrued knowledge. Research clearly shows that vocabulary improves with time.”
Vocabulary 就是這種累積知識的一種專門形式。研究清楚顯示，vocabulary 會隨時間改善。
選項 C 說 vocabulary 作為 crystallised intelligence 的一種形式，隨年齡下降很少。原文說得更強：vocabulary improves with time，且 crystallized intelligence 至少到 75 歲前不下降。C 雖然用

“declines very little” 表達得較保守，但它最能概括作者放入 vocabulary research 的功能。選項排除A Some people are more sensitive to vocabulary than others.原文沒有討論 sensitivity to vocabulary。 B Teachers and other professionals benefit from experience.這只是最後一句的例子。作者提到 retired teachers and journalists，是為了證明 vocabulary 和accrued knowledge 會隨時間累積，B 的範圍太窄。 D Older people use a specialised area of the brain when studying. Paragraph J 沒有說 specialised brain area。所以 30 答案是 C。

questions.prompt: It has long been believed that 31 ______ declines with age.
questions.translation: 長久以來，人們相信 ______ 會隨年齡下降。

blocks.text: 主要目標段落：Paragraph E背景也可回看 Paragraph A，因為 A 段先介紹傳統老化觀點。
“One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory—notorious for its failure with age.”
最重要的 mental functions 之一是 memory，而 memory 又以隨年齡失效聞名。
“That event is etched into your episodic memory.”
那個事件會刻入你的 episodic memory。
只看首尾句，Paragraph E 的功能是把全文焦點集中到 memory，並開始區分 memory 的不同形式。題目第一句說 “declines with age”，自然要找 E 段中 “failure with age” 這類說法。
“memory and other mental functions deteriorate over time”
題目需要一個名詞，放在 “that ______ declines with age” 中。最直接、最自然的名詞是 memory。
“One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory—notorious for its failure with age.”
最重要的心理功能之一是記憶，而記憶又以隨年齡失效聞名。
這句中的 “memory” 是主語核心；“failure with age” 對應題目 “declines with age”。另外Paragraph A 說：
“In humans, psychologists concluded, memory and other mental functions deteriorate over time because of inevitable organic changes in the brain as neurons die off.”
在人類方面，心理學家曾下結論：memory 和其他 mental functions 會隨時間退化，原因是neurons 死亡造成大腦中不可避免的 organic changes。
題目把 “failure with age / deteriorate over time” 改寫成 “declines with age”。空格需要 one/two words from passage。答案用一個詞 memory，文法和意思都正確。

questions.prompt: The Charles A. Dana Foundation invested millions of dollars in studying memory loss, using advanced technology, neurochemical experiments, and cognitive and 32 ______ tests.
questions.translation: Charles A. Dana Foundation 投放數百萬美元研究 memory loss，使用先進科技、neurochemical experiments，以及 cognitive and ______ tests。

blocks.text: “One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory—notorious for its failure with age.”
最重要的 mental functions 之一是 memory，而 memory 又以隨年齡失效聞名。
“That event is etched into your episodic memory.”
那個事件會刻入你的 episodic memory。
Paragraph E 介紹 memory loss research 和 memory types。題目出現 “Charles A. Dana Foundation”，這是非常強的定位詞，答案應在 E 段前半部。
掃描時不需要讀完整段，只要找專有名詞 Charles A. Dana Foundation，很快會看到完整串列。

“So important is memory that the Charles A. Dana Foundation recently spent $8.4 million to set up a consortium of leading medical centers to measure memory loss and aging through brain imaging technology, neurochemical experiments, and cognitive and psychological tests.”

Memory 如此重要，以至於 Charles A. Dana Foundation 最近花了 840 萬美元，建立一個由頂尖medical centers 組成的 consortium，透過 brain imaging technology、neurochemical experiments，以及 cognitive and psychological tests 來測量 memory loss 和 aging。
題目幾乎照原文順序改寫。

“invested millions of dollars” 對應 “spent $8.4 million”。“advanced technology” 對應 “brain imaging technology”。“cognitive and 32 ______ tests” 對應 “cognitive and psychological tests”。空格前有 “cognitive and”，後面有 “tests”，所以答案應是形容詞，修飾 tests。原文詞是psychological。所以 32 答案是 psychological。

questions.prompt: Bahrick called one form of memory “33 ______”, which stores factual knowledge.
questions.translation: Bahrick 把其中一種 memory 稱為 “______”，它儲存 factual knowledge。

blocks.text: “One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory—notorious for its failure with age.”
最重要的 mental functions 之一是 memory，而 memory 又以隨年齡失效聞名。
“That event is etched into your episodic memory.”
那個事件會刻入你的 episodic memory。
Paragraph E 後半開始分類 memory。題目問 factual knowledge 的 memory form，因此要找
“Bahrick” 是人名定位詞；“facts” 是答案附近的語義定位詞。
關鍵原文：“What we call knowledge—facts—is what psychologists such as Harry P. Bahrick, Ph.D., of Ohio Wesleyan University call semantic memory.”
我們所稱的 knowledge，即 facts，是 Ohio Wesleyan University 的 Harry P. Bahrick 等心理學家稱為 semantic memory 的東西。
題目把 “knowledge—facts” 改寫成 “factual knowledge”。原文直接說這類 knowledge/facts 叫semantic memory。答案必須取自原文，且 NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS，因此 semantic memory 完全符合。
不要只填 “semantic”，因為題目問 one form of memory；完整術語是 semantic memory。
所以 33 答案是 semantic memory。

questions.prompt: Another form, “34 ______”, contains events situated in time and space.
questions.translation: 另一種 memory，稱為 “______”，包含位於特定時間和空間中的 events。

blocks.text: “One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory—notorious for its failure with age.”
最重要的 mental functions 之一是 memory，而 memory 又以隨年齡失效聞名。
“That event is etched into your episodic memory.”
那個事件會刻入你的 episodic memory。
首尾句顯示這段後半會討論 episodic memory。題目說 “events situated in time and space”，這幾乎是 E 段中相關句子的改寫。
“Events, conversations, and occurrences in time and space”
“time and space” 是非常強的原文定位詞，掃描 E 段可直接找到答案句。
關鍵原文：“Events, conversations, and occurrences in time and space, on the other hand, make up episodic or event memory, which is triggered by cues from the context.”
另一方面，events、conversations，以及位於 time and space 中的 occurrences，構成 episodic或 event memory；這類記憶由 context 中的 cues 觸發。
題目中的 “contains events situated in time and space” 對應原文 “Events, conversations, and occurrences in time and space … make up”。
空格需要 memory form。原文提供兩個可接受名稱：episodic memory / event memory。由於前一題是 semantic memory，這一題通常配對為 episodic memory。它也在段落最後一句再次出現。
所以 34 答案是 episodic memory。

questions.prompt: To investigate the longevity of knowledge, he asked 1,000 participants about 35 ______; some could still remember the subject decades after studying it.
questions.translation: 為了研究 knowledge 的持久性，他向 1,000 名參與者詢問 ______；有些人在學習該科多年後仍記得。

blocks.text: “Probing the longevity of knowledge, Bahrick tested 1,000 high school graduates to see how well they recalled their algebra.”
為了探查 knowledge 的持久性，Bahrick 測試了 1,000 名 high school graduates，看他們對algebra 的回憶程度。
“Those who had spent only a few months learning algebra forgot most of it within two or three years.”
那些只花幾個月學 algebra 的人，在兩三年內便忘記大部分。
首尾句都出現 algebra。題目也說 “1,000 participants” 和 “longevity of knowledge”，所以答案位置非常明確。
掃描 Paragraph G 第一、二句即可定位。
“Probing the longevity of knowledge, Bahrick tested 1,000 high school graduates to see how well they recalled their algebra.”
為了探查 knowledge 的持久性，Bahrick 測試 1,000 名 high school graduates，看他們能回憶起多少 algebra。
題目的 “asked 1,000 participants about” 是對 “tested 1,000 high school graduates to see how well they recalled” 的概括。空格問 subject，所以答案是原文學科名稱 algebra。
這題要注意答案形式。原文有 “their algebra”，但填空句已經是 “about ______”，只需要 subject名稱。填 “their algebra” 會不自然；答案表通常接受 algebra。

questions.prompt: A second study of Spanish courses found that people who took several courses could recall more than half of the 36 ______ they had learned decades later, whereas those who took only one course retained very little after three years.
questions.translation: 另一個 Spanish courses 研究發現，修讀多門課的人，數十年後仍可記得超過一半他們學過的______；只修一門課的人三年後只保留很少。

blocks.text: “In another study, Bahrick discovered that people who had taken several courses in Spanish, spread out over a couple of years, could recall, decades later, 60 percent or more of the vocabulary they learned.”
在另一項研究中，Bahrick 發現，那些在幾年間分散修讀數門 Spanish courses 的人，數十年後仍能回憶起他們學過 vocabulary 的 60% 或以上。
“No serious deficit appears until people get to their 50s and 60s, probably due to the degenerative processes of aging rather than a cognitive loss.”
直到人們進入五、六十歲前，通常不會出現嚴重缺損；若出現，可能來自老化的退化過程，較少可視為單純 cognitive loss。
第一句已直接提供答案。這段功能是用 Spanish vocabulary 研究延續 algebra study，說明長期知識 residue 可保持多年。
“more than half” 對應 “60 percent or more”。空格應填一個名詞，表示學過並能記得的內容。

關鍵原文：“In another study, Bahrick discovered that people who had taken several courses in Spanish, spread out over a couple of years, could recall, decades later, 60 percent or more of the vocabulary they learned.”
在另一項研究中，Bahrick 發現，在幾年間分散修讀數門 Spanish courses 的人，數十年後仍能記起所學 vocabulary 的 60% 或以上。
題目中的 “more than half” 是 “60 percent or more” 的改寫。
“the ______ they had learned” 對應 “the vocabulary they learned”。答案直接取原文一個詞vocabulary。所以 36 答案是 vocabulary。

questions.prompt: Examined cerebral blood flow in both young and old people during a test
questions.translation: 在一項測試中，檢查年輕人和老年人的 cerebral blood flow。

blocks.text: “Equipped with imaging techniques that capture the brain in action, Stanley Rapoport, Ph.D., at the National Institutes of Health, measured the flow of blood in the brains of old and young people as they went through the task of matching photos of faces.”
National Institutes of Health 的 Stanley Rapoport 配備能捕捉大腦活動的 imaging techniques，測量老年人和年輕人在進行 matching photos of faces 任務時的大腦血流。

“Either the task required greater effort on the part of the older subjects or the work of neurons originally involved in tasks of that type had been taken over by other neurons, creating different networks.”
這可能表示該任務對老年受試者需要更大努力，或者原先負責這類任務的 neurons 的工作已由其他 neurons 接手，形成不同 networks。
第一句已同時出現人名 Stanley Rapoport、blood flow、old and young people、test/task。這段就是答案段落。
“measured the flow of blood in the brains”
“cerebral” 等於 brain-related；題目把 “flow of blood in the brains” 改寫成 “cerebral blood flow”。
關鍵原文：“Stanley Rapoport, Ph.D., at the National Institutes of Health, measured the flow of blood in the brains of old and young people as they went through the task of matching photos of faces.”
National Institutes of Health 的 Stanley Rapoport 測量老年人和年輕人在進行 matching photos of faces 任務時的大腦血流。
題目中的 “Examined cerebral blood flow” 對應 “measured the flow of blood in the brains”。
“both young and old people” 對應 “old and young people”。“during a test” 對應 “as they went through the task of matching photos of faces”。人物列表中 Stanley Rapoport 是 E。所以 37 答案是 E。

questions.prompt: Explained that ageing reflects the interaction between physical and mental activity
questions.translation: 解釋 aging 反映身體活動和心理活動之間的互動。

blocks.text: “Aging, it is now clear, is part of an ongoing maturation process that all our organs go through.”
現在已清楚，aging 是所有器官都會經歷的 ongoing maturation process 的一部分。
“Mental decline after young adulthood appeared inevitable.”
young adulthood 之後的 mental decline 看起來似乎不可避免。
Paragraph A 建立關於 aging、body、mind、brain 的傳統和研究背景。題目有 “physical and mental activity interaction”，這正好對應 Scheibel 引文。
“continuous interaction between levels of body activity and levels of mental activity”
“physical activity” 在原文表達成 “body activity”。人物在引文後立即出現：Arnold B. Scheibel。
關鍵原文：“‘In a sense, aging is keyed to the level of vigor of the body and the continuous interaction between levels of body activity and levels of mental activity,’ reports Arnold B. Scheibel, M.D.”
Arnold B. Scheibel 報告說：「在某種意義上，aging 取決於身體活力水平，以及 body activity levels 和 mental activity levels 之間的持續互動。」題目說 “ageing reflects the interaction between physical and mental activity”。
“physical activity” 對應原文 “body activity”。“mental activity” 原字重現。“reflects the interaction” 對應 “is keyed to … the continuous interaction”。人物列表中 Arnold B. Scheibel 是 B。所以 38 答案是 B。

questions.prompt: Explained that repeated episodic memories can become semantic memories
questions.translation: 解釋重複的 episodic memories 可以變成 semantic memories。

blocks.text: “When you forget a less vivid item, like buying a roll of paper towels at the supermarket, you may blame it on your aging memory.”
當你忘記較不鮮明的事情，例如在超市買一卷 paper towels，你可能會把它歸咎於 aging memory。
“Our language knowledge, our knowledge of the world and of people, is largely that permanent or semipermanent residue.”
我們的 language knowledge、world knowledge 和 people knowledge，大多就是那種 permanent或 semipermanent residue。
Paragraph F 的功能是解釋 event memory 如何透過 repetition 轉成 knowledge residue。題目同時出現 episodic memory 和 semantic memory，因此要找 Bahrick 對兩者轉換的說法。
“What started as an episodic memory has become a permanent part of your knowledge base”
“Through repetition” 是最重要定位詞，因為題目說 repeated。
關鍵原文：“‘Every memory begins as an event,’ says Bahrick. ‘Through repetition, certain events leave behind a residue of knowledge, or semantic memory.’”
Bahrick 說：「每個 memory 都始於一個 event。透過 repetition，某些 events 會留下 knowledge的 residue，也就是 semantic memory。」再看下一句：
“What started as an episodic memory has become a permanent part of your knowledge base.”
原本作為 episodic memory 開始的東西，已經成為你 knowledge base 中永久的一部分。
題目說 “repeated episodic memories can become semantic memories”。原文把這條轉換說得很清楚：event → repetition → residue of knowledge / semantic memory。人物是 Bahrick。
人物列表中 Harry P. Bahrick 是 A。

questions.prompt: Showed that a rat’s brain develops in a stimulating environment
questions.translation: 顯示 rat’s brain 在 stimulating environment 中會發展。

blocks.text: “When a rat is kept in isolation without playmates or objects to interact with, the animal’s brain shrinks, but if we put that rat with 11 other rats in a large cage and give them an assortment of wheels, ladders, and other toys, we can show—after four days—significant differences in its brain,” says Diamond, professor of integrative biology.
Diamond 說，如果老鼠被孤立飼養，沒有玩伴或互動物件，牠的大腦會縮小；但若把牠和另外 11隻老鼠放入大籠，並提供 wheels、ladders 和其他 toys，四天後就可看到大腦有顯著差異。最後一句：“Animals are just like we are. They need stimulation,” says Diamond.
Diamond 說，動物和我們一樣。牠們需要 stimulation。首尾句直接連到 rat、brain、stimulation。題目問 rat’s brain develops in stimulating environment，因此 Paragraph D 是目標段落。
“stimulating environment” 在原文中主要對應 “enriched environment” 和 “need stimulation”。
關鍵原文：“After a month in the enriched environment, the whole cerebral cortex has expanded, as has its blood supply.”
在 enriched environment 中一個月後，整個 cerebral cortex 已擴大，血液供應也增加。
integrative biology 教授 Diamond 說。
題目中的 “brain develops” 對應 “cerebral cortex has expanded” 和 “blood supply” 增加。
“stimulating environment” 對應 “enriched environment”，即有同伴、大籠、wheels、ladders 和toys 的環境。文章只稱她為 Diamond；人物列表提供全名 Marion Diamond，選項是 C。所以 40 答案是 C。

paragraphOverview.title: 全文 Skim Roadmap
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph A 首句說 aging 是所有器官都會經歷的 ongoing maturation process，並引入 Arnold Scheibel 對身體活力和心理活動互動的說法。尾句說 mental decline after young adulthood appeared inevitable。只看首尾句，可以先估計這段在介紹舊觀念：老化會帶來大腦、記憶和心理功能衰退。段落功能偏向建立傳統假設，為後文的新研究和修正觀點鋪路。

Paragraph B 首句提到 Stanley Rapoport 用 imaging techniques 觀察 old and young people 在matching photos of faces 時的大腦血流。尾句提出兩種可能：老人完成任務需要更多努力，或其他 neurons 接手原來神經元的工作。只看首尾句，這段大概會用腦部影像研究說明：老年人可達到同樣表現，但使用的 neural networks 可能不同。

Paragraph C 首句介紹 Timothy Salthouse 比較年輕打字員和六十多歲打字員。尾句說 typing 相關的 neural networks 似乎已 reshaped，以補償 motor skills 或其他年齡變化的損失。只看首尾句，可以推測這段用 typists experiment 證明 older adults 可能靠經驗策略維持表現，例如減少手指動作、預讀文字，從而補償反應和動作速度下降。
Paragraph D 首句說 isolated rat 的 brain shrinks，但放入有同伴和玩具的大籠後，四天內已可看到大腦差異。尾句說 animals 和 humans 一樣需要 stimulation。只看首尾句，這段重點非常清楚：環境刺激會影響腦部發展。孤立、單調環境對大腦不利；豐富、變化和社交環境可以促進dendrites、cortex 和 blood supply 的發展。

Paragraph E 首句把焦點轉向 memory，說它是極重要但以隨年齡失效聞名的 mental function。尾句用 JFK assassination 作例，說重大事件會刻入 episodic memory。只看首尾句，這段會介紹memory research，尤其 Charles A. Dana Foundation 的研究，以及 semantic memory 和episodic memory 的分類：一類儲存事實知識，一類儲存特定時間和空間中的事件。

Paragraph F 首句說人們忘記 supermarket 買 paper towels 這類不鮮明事件時，可能會怪 aging memory。尾句說 language knowledge、world knowledge 和 people knowledge 大多是permanent or semipermanent residue。只看首尾句，這段會解釋 episodic memory 如何透過repetition 變成 semantic memory。它也把一般健忘和長期知識保留分開處理。

Paragraph G 首句說 Bahrick 測試 1,000 名 high school graduates，看他們記得多少 algebra。尾句說只學幾個月 algebra 的人，兩三年內會忘記大部分。只看首尾句，這段集中研究知識持久性：記得多少 algebra 主要取決於學習時間長短，而非離開課程多久。這段是 education/duration of instruction 影響長期記憶的核心例子。
Paragraph H 首句說 Bahrick 另一研究發現，修讀數門 Spanish courses 且分散在幾年內的人，數十年後仍可記得 60% 或以上 vocabulary。尾句說嚴重缺損通常到五、六十歲後才出現，較可能來自退化過程。只看首尾句，這段延續 Paragraph G：長期知識 residue 可穩定多年，語言詞彙保留和學習量、課程分布有密切關係。

Paragraph I 首句由 Robert Kail 談 metamemory，說它可視作 going to school 的副產品。尾句解釋 child chess experts 記棋盤較好，因為他們的 chess knowledge organized better，並成為 new memory 的 framework。只看首尾句，這段會說教育和專門知識如何幫助記憶。記憶表現不單靠年齡，也取決於已有知識是否有組織。

Paragraph J 首句說 specialized knowledge 是會隨時間改善的 mental resource。尾句說 retired professionals，尤其 teachers and journalists，在 vocabulary 和 general information tests 中通常比 college students 得分更高。只看首尾句，這段是全文結尾：專門知識、crystallized intelligence、chunking、expertise 和 vocabulary 都顯示，某些能力會靠經驗累積，並不會在成年後迅速下降。
